observations: body L1: the o of «considera-» is covered by a blot.

body L1-L11: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the sphere (radius 59.5 pt), the meridian AEB, the equator CED, the ecliptic from G through H and the first point of Aries to F, and the arc KLC from K to C, as arcs of circles fitted to the print (radius 408.5, 212.3, 179.1 and 63.8 pt); the centre of the arc KLC lies 0.5 pt from H, its pole. The words «ecliptica» and «aequator» run along their circles; the sign of Aries stands over the meeting of the ecliptic and the equator.

body L3, L9: «Menelai» is letter-spaced in L3, not in L9. Menelaus' theorem is stated on p. 192, in Schiaparelli's addition to the notes on chapter 18. The sign of Aries is printed «♈» in L4 and in the formulas.

body L5-L12: H is the pole of KLC, so HK and HL are quadrants; C, on the equator 90° from E, is a pole of the meridian, so KC is a quadrant and KL measures the angle LHE. The theorem of Menelaus for the triangle HKL cut by the equator, which meets HK in E, HL in ♈ and KL produced in C, gives L11; with HE = δ, EK = 90° − δ, H♈ = λ, ♈L = 90° − λ and LC = 90° − KL it becomes L12, that is cos ang. lat. = R tan δ : tan λ, formula (α) of p. 258. The comma after L11 is printed high, beside the tops of the denominators; in L12 the bar after «90°» (9.8 pt, as long as the signs of equality) is a minus sign.
body L13: the dash after «q)» measures 10.2 pt, the hyphen of «5-8» 3.2 pt.

body L14-L22: the place is p. 82, L5-L8 («nam arcus horizontis inter ortum gradus ascendentis et directionem gradus dati in horizonte est ut quantitas anguli latitudinis»). The hyphen of «colligun-» stands high; a speck prints before «tur» (L15) and another in the margin before L17. Heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition; «al–Battānī» (L18) has a long dash (5.4 pt), the dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 9.2 pt.
body L23: the dash after «r)» measures 10.2 pt, the hyphen of «8-26» 3.5 pt.

body L24-L29: the a of «distantiae» (L24) prints broken; the dash after «zenithalis.» (L26) measures 10.2 pt; «al–Battānī» (L28) has a long dash (5.9 pt). The z of the zenith distance of the Moon (L27, L29) is printed as a tailed italic z. «adn. h, p. 256»: ζ is computed by formula (α) of note i), p. 256, L34; note h) there (L7) concerns the distance of the Sun. (α) is al-Battānī's rule of p. 82, L13-L21: the arc whose sine is sin β sin ang. lat. : R taken from ζ when the Moon lies toward the zenith from the ecliptic, added to it otherwise; the derivation and Schiaparelli's comparison with the exact rule follow on p. 260.

body L30-L40: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the ecliptic GA, a flat arc (radius 1185 pt) beginning left of the margin; the vertical circles ZT, ZK and ZD, arcs of circles fitted to the print through the apex Z (radius 153.6, 171.3 and 167.7 pt); the circle of latitude EBD and the perpendiculars EL and KD, straight strokes; the stroke from the pole Q to E in eight dashes, the last joined to E. «370–72» (L31) has a long dash (5.5 pt).

body L38-L40: the triangles ELB and BKD, right-angled at L and K, have equal hypotenuses EB = BD = β and equal vertical angles at B, so EL = DK; the law of sines (p. 181, note 1) gives sin EL = sin EB sin EBL : R, with EBL the angle of longitude: as printed.
